title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 8: electing the corrupt mass — no duty to choose the majority
pass_a_gloss: Further, this also is to be observed, that we speak of the election to life of those who are all most worthy of eternal death. Although therefore we admit that God from the goodness of his nature wills to all human beings, inasmuch as they are considered before the fall adorned with justice and holiness, that gift of eternal life; yet no reason compels us to say that, from human beings corrupted and sunk in the damnable mass, God for his goodness owes it to elect either all, or the greater part, to glory.
pass_b_english: Further: we are speaking of election to life of people who are all most worthy of eternal death. We may grant that from the goodness of his nature God wills the gift of eternal life to all humans as considered before the fall, adorned with justice and holiness — yet no reason forces us to say that, from humans corrupted and sunk in the damnable mass, his goodness obliges him to elect either all or the greater part to glory.
source_text: Porro, illud quoque observandum nos loqui de electione eorum ad vitam, qui sunt omnes morte aeterna dignissimi. Quamvis igitur admittamus Deum ex bonitate suae naturae velle omnibus hominibus, quatenus considerantur ante lapsum justitia et sanctitate ornati, donum illud aeternae vitae; nulla tamen ratio cogit ut dicamus, ex hominibus corruptis et in massa damnabili obrutis, Deum pro bonitate sua debere vel omnes, vel majorem partem eligere ad gloriam.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. III Rat. 8 section 309. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap3_rat8_densify. Honest partial.
